audit.why: 4/10 with Trundle taking all seven stages is right and matches the 54.71% over 223 games: Cho'Gath has no dash, no escape, a 6s telegraphed Rupture and a 300-range silence, all of which lose to a champion who wants a long melee fight on his own terrain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike says 'Cho'Gath's Feast and armor/MR stacking peak here, and Subjugate strips exactly that' but never states the reason this is the best Subjugate target in the game — Subjugate steals a percent of HEALTH as well as armour and MR, and the steal doubles over 4 seconds.
audit.why: Riot's Subjugate text: 'immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance. Over the next 4 seconds the amount stolen is doubled.' Riot's Feast text: 'If the target is killed, Cho'Gath grows, gaining maximum Health.' A percent steal against the largest health bar on the map is the biggest single R payout Trundle can get.
audit.corrected: Spike now states the percent-of-Health steal and the 4-second doubling as the reason to open the all-in with R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four things. (a) The ability is labelled 'Rupture (Knockup)' throughout — the name is Rupture, and the parenthetical reads as part of the name. (b) breakdown.cooldowns lists Rupture twice, once under each label. (c) Feral Scream is never named anywhere despite dontsFull[1] warning about being 'silenced mid-cast'. (d) The late block claims Feast 'deals true damage proportional to his current stats' and that Heartsteel Cho'Gath 'ignores your healing entirely' — neither is in Riot's text and neither is true. (e) early says 'his attack speed is debuffed by your Q' — Chomp saps Attack Damage, not attack speed.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon: Rupture, 6s, 950 range, 'Ruptures the ground at target location, popping enemy units into the air'. Feral Scream, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, 300 range, 'Silencing enemies for a few seconds' — the same reach as Chomp, so if you are close enough to bite you are close enough to be silenced. Feast, 80/70/60, 175 range, 'dealing a high amount of true damage' — true damage, which is why the armour Subjugate steals does nothing against it, but nothing about proportional scaling or healing denial.
audit.corrected: Name fixed to Rupture with its 6s cooldown, the duplicate cooldown line collapsed, Feral Scream named with its 11s and 300 range, and the two invented Feast mechanics removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rupture is the tracked ability everywhere with no duration attached, and the second-most punishing cooldown in the lane is never mentioned.
audit.why: Rupture is 6s — short, so you cannot simply wait it out; you sidestep it. Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1 and that is the real window: with the silence gone he cannot stop a Chomp-into-Pillar sequence at all.
audit.corrected: 6s and 11s now stated in the cooldown block and the report.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Cho'Gath to deny disengage, or between you and Rupture (Knockup) to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar closes the kit — Cho'Gath has no dash at all, so terrain behind him after he steps up is a wall he cannot cross.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's lane power plateau kicks in around level 6 when Feast goes online — his raw HP stack and true-damage execute mean he can threaten your all-ins with the threat of R. The critical shift here: stop thinking about trading freely and start treating every all-in as a Subjugate timing. Cast R on him the moment you engage so the drained armor and MR stack onto you for the full fight duration; a Cho with 100 armor becomes your 100 armor mid-skirmish. Hold Pillar to block his path AFTER the R lands so he cannot flash or stumble out of your domain. Between levels 4 and 5, before you hit 6, respect Rupture as your lane-ender — he will try to land it when you step forward for Q, so trade only when his Q is visibly on cooldown and keep enough HP that a knockup into follow-up auto does not decide the lane.

edits.before: Two-plus items is where Cho'Gath starts winning the arms race he was always trying to win — Feast stacks, AP items, and his true-damage R begin to outpace what Subjugate drains. His R does not care about the armor you stole; it deals true damage proportional to his current stats, and a 6-stack Cho'Gath with Heartsteel ignores your healing entirely with one button. Do not take solo fights unless Subjugate is up and he is below half HP. Your real late-game value is in 5v5: drain their tanky frontliner with R in every team fight, use Pillar to peel or zone their engage tools, and let your resistance snowball support your backline. The matchup never flips to even in a straight 1v1 if he has full items — play around team fights and your R cooldown rather than trying to settle it in lane again.
edits.after: Two-plus items is where Cho'Gath starts winning the arms race he was always trying to win — Feast stacks, AP items, and his true-damage R begin to outpace what Subjugate drains. edits.after: Feast is live and its true damage ignores every point of armour Subjugate steals — he now threatens a kill off a knockup into R, so only all-in immediately after Rupture whiffs, with Subjugate already cast.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's early game is genuinely weak — low base damage, telegraphed Q, and no real escape — and you are built to exploit exactly that. Start Chomp and bite him on every CS attempt; the AD steal is immediate and his base MR is low, so every trade chips him while King's Tribute refunds HP off dying minions without burning a single ability. He will try to keep max range and use Rupture to punish your step-ups: that ground spike is slow but the knockup interrupts your Frozen Domain, so read the animation and sidestep before committing W. Drop the ice zone at your feet only after you confirm his Q is on cooldown — then he has no way out, his attack speed is debuffed by your Q, and you are healing faster than his passive regeneration can offset. At level 3 you can add Pillar behind him after a trade to deny disengage; a trapped Cho'Gath with no Q is a free chunk before the wave resets.

notes: 'Rupture (Knockup)' was being used as the ability's name across the full layer, including a duplicated cooldown line that listed the same spell twice; replaced with 'Rupture (6s)' so the real name carries the real cooldown. Feral Scream (11s, 300-range cone silence) was never named anywhere even though the don'ts warned about being silenced — it is now named with the detail that matters, that its 300 range is exactly Chomp's range. Removed two invented Feast mechanics from the late block: it does not deal damage 'proportional to his current stats' and Heartsteel does not make him 'ignore your healing'. The genuinely valuable and previously unstated point is that Subjugate steals a percent of HEALTH as well as resists, which makes the game's biggest health-stacker its best R target.
